text:
maya: Heads-up — gpu-watchdog reported intermittent ECC/Xid patterns on 2 cards in eu-west1-3. Thinking of running a preflight probe that does a soft-isolate of the card, runs a quick memtest + short workload, then either unquarantine or trigger a graceful node drain across K8s+Slurm. Any red flags?
simon: +1 for preflight probe. prefer soft-isolate first (no full node eviction). Can we avoid immediate force-restart? :slightly_smiling_face:
li-wei: what's the probe runtime? we need to keep it < 90s to not blow the autoscaler billing. also need to maintain prefix KV cache for active sessions.
maya: probe = 60s memtest + 20s synthetic token gen (~80s). If pass -> unquarantine; if fail -> mark card quarantined and schedule soft-cordon for that GPU's pod/partition.
eva: how will soft-cordon interact with slurm ephemeral allocation? we have a bunch of older batch jobs pinned to that node.
simon: plan: for slurm, signal set GPUTAINT on node and create drain window with backoff. For k8s, kubectl cordon + kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120. Keep batch jobs a priority: try to allow running jobs to finish unless they exceed a 10m hard cutoff.
thomas: cost note — if we start evicting a lot in eu-west1, autoscaler will spin up new nodes (spot fallback -> on-demand). can we prefer cross-region fallback before on-demand? region-aware routing might be slower but cheaper.
maya: good call. propose routing policy: 1) same AZ spare GPU pool, 2) cross-AZ in region, 3) cross-region (eu-west2), 4) on-demand fallback. Also add cost threshold: if predicted extra cost > $X/hr then trigger paging.
gpu-watchdog-bot: [alert] 2 cards flagged: gpu=ga102-6, node=node-eu-3-47. ECC spike @ 21:07 UTC. Recent Xid burst 12m window > 3. Suggested action: PRELIGHT_ISOLATE -> MEMTEST -> QUARANTINE/UNQUARANTINE.
ops-bot: ran dry-run of orchestration earlier today. sample command: 
```
/drain-orch start --node node-eu-3-47 --mode soft-cordon --probe memtest:80s --slurm-grace 600 --k8s-grace 120
```
li-wei: that looks fine. please ensure the probe writes health signals to /sys/gpu/quarantine and emits metric gpu.quarantine.preflight.[pass|fail]. we use those counters to avoid thrash (hysteresis).
eva: also add a cooldown per-card of 6h and a retry budget of 2 probes before forcing replacement. we've seen flaky cards flipflop and create churning drains.
simon: agree — hysteresis details: require 2 consecutive fail probes within 30m OR Xid rate > 10/min for 5m to auto-replace. otherwise keep quarantined + schedule maintenance ticket.
maya: what about user-visible SLOs? need to mark routes behind model-pool as degraded and temporarily divert low-priority traffic to smaller quantized model to maintain latency.
thomas: ops-cost override: if eviction leads to > $200/hr extra, ops team gets paged and automatic cross-region is paused until manual ack.
li-wei: corner case: if memtest passes but Xid bursts continue on live workload, we should capture live traces (perf counters + nv-hostengine logs) and escalate. add a short live-run probe by replaying a recent trace for 30s.
maya: will add live-run probe flag to drain-orch: --live-replay 30s. default off.
simon: one more — make sure preflight probe doesn't trigger model cache invalidation. add header to replay requests: `X-Inference-Probe: true` so downstream caches treat differently.
gpu-watchdog-bot: noted. enqueue maintenance case: #M-4829, assigned to infra-queue.
ops-bot: scheduling rollout: start with canary: 1 node in eu-west1-3, wait 15m, then 10% of affected nodes, watch cpu/gpu utilization + failed evictions. use metric  `infra.drain.fail_rate` < 1% to proceed.
emma (observer): curious — are we persisting KV caches across soft-cordon? some models drop token cache if pod restarts. we should prefer migrating warm pods before eviction.
maya: good point. drain-orch will attempt live-migrate pods with active GPU sessions using our session-proxy (TTL 120s). if migration fails, mark for graceful eviction only after user-specified grace.
li-wei: ok i'm happy to greenlight canary config. i'll update the probe implementation and add the metrics + cooldown.
simon: I'll update the runbooks with the new thresholds and add the cross-region billing guard.
maya: thanks all. i'll kick off a canary at 22:30 UTC and post results. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: canary scheduled at 22:30 UTC. environment=prod, region=eu-west1-3, nodes=1. monitor dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/evac/soft-isolate-canary
gpu-watchdog-bot: follow-up in thread when probe completes.
